## a departure report compares the change with its plan

ID: `plan-run/a-departure-report-compares-the-change-with-its-plan`

Status: **implemented and tested**

The departure report SHALL list every file changed in commits since `REF` whose repository-relative path does not appear in the change's `tasks.md` as read from `REF` and is neither the `path` of a `layout:` row in `lockstep.yaml` as read from `REF` nor a file one of those rows names in its `tests:`, excluding files under `openspec/`, the OpenSpec spec links `make docs-specs` writes under `docs/specs/`, `lockstep.yaml` itself and the generated `docs/links.json`, and every task line still unticked in the change's `tasks.md` at the branch head, read from `openspec/changes/<change>/` or, once archived, from the latest `openspec/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<change>/`. It reports and never blocks.

## hidden acceptance tests are written before and run after implementation

ID: `plan-run/hidden-acceptance-tests-are-written-before-and-run-after-implementation`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`lockstep accept write <change>` SHALL run one headless agent session, in a detached worktree at `REF` that is removed afterwards and with no session history kept on disk, that writes pytest files into the run folder outside every worktree, and SHALL then run those tests once at `REF` and record the result. `lockstep accept check <change>` SHALL, in the implementer's worktree, count uncommitted files, copy the hidden tests into `tests/` without overwriting any file, run the test command, remove the copies, run the check command, write the departure report, and record the head commit, all results and the transcripts in the run folder's `summary.json`. Neither command merges. The hidden-run result SHALL preserve the test command exit status and report the passed, failed, error and skipped counts from a fresh pytest JUnit report for the copied tests. `lockstep accept check` and `lockstep run-plan` SHALL require exit 0, at least one passing hidden case and zero failures or errors before returning success. When the invocation produces a report, Lockstep SHALL keep the report beside the corresponding log and name it in the receipt. When the invocation produces no report, the receipt SHALL identify no report and earlier reports SHALL NOT count as evidence for it. A missing or unreadable report, no tests or an all-skipped run SHALL fail the acceptance check. A custom `--test-cmd` SHALL continue to receive the copied filenames as arguments and must run pytest with the supplied `PYTEST_ADDOPTS` environment so the check can read its report.

## one driver runs a plan with claude or codex

ID: `plan-run/one-driver-runs-a-plan-with-claude-or-codex`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`lockstep run-plan <change> --agent claude|codex` SHALL run `accept write`, then one headless implementer session in a new worktree on branch `impl/<change>-<run id>`, then `accept check`, saving each session's JSON event stream as its transcript, and SHALL print the `ship` command to run next without running it: `uv run ship` when the repository's `pyproject.toml` depends on `agentic-engineering-system` (which installs `ship`), else `ship`. The agent choice SHALL change only the command that starts each session.

## the agents are told to lay out the planned files

ID: `plan-run/the-agents-are-told-to-lay-out-the-planned-files`

Status: **implemented and tested**

The implementer's prompt and the acceptance-test writer's prompt SHALL say that when `lockstep.yaml` has `layout:` rows, those rows name the files the plan creates or changes, with their exports; the implementer's prompt SHALL tell it to run `uv run lockstep layout` before writing code, so each new planned file starts with its requirement text.
